answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake before it may trade, like a beekeeper guarding nectar: each agent posts a bond that is slashed on fraud, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand bonds. Honest agents earn the bond back with interest, while an attacker who floods the market burns capital faster than the island of real users can be overwhelmed — and like a willow that bends but holds its ground, the system stays standing because faking scale is priced out of reach.
